meta.title: The Truthful Balloon
meta.blurb: You inherit a half-finished sky map and a balloon that rises only when someone tells it the truth. Your first delivery waits beyond an uncharted bank of cloud, and the old route leaves something unsaid.
meta.author: ohnna with ChatGPT

world: Harbors on tall sea cliffs trade with small inhabited sky islands using patched balloons, weather vanes, brass instruments and canvas docks. The apprentice inherits their mentor's unfinished map and a balloon whose stitched envelope tightens only around a freely offered truth believed by its speaker. Ordinary, non-private truths work; uncertainty can be admitted; repetition is not an infinite fuel supply because each new stage of flight needs an honest observation or intention relevant to that stage. Lies slacken the canvas and force a controlled landing at the nearest safe mooring, never a fatal plunge. The missing map section reflects the mentor's unacknowledged mistake about a community's route. The narrator knows this rule but reveals the history through evidence and conversation, not forced confession.
tone: Bright salt air, patched canvas, brisk discovery and capable companions. Honest uncertainty and practical teamwork matter. A wrong bearing means a safe mooring and another try, never a fatal fall.
playerRole: You are a cartographer's apprentice who has inherited a half-finished sky map and a balloon that rises only for freely offered truth. You carry a map tube, charcoal, brass sighting compass, rope and a packed lunch. You choose your own name and what you are willing to say.
narratorStyle: Second-person present with legible geography, wind and rope details. Ask before committing the player to a statement. Ordinary observations and admitted uncertainty can provide lift; never demand private confession or invent a player secret. Keep momentum through choices in route, evidence and responsibility, not combat or hidden truth scores.

cast.name: Ren
cast.appearance: A lean adult of mixed Black and white heritage with a dark braided undercut, hazel eyes, sun-browned medium-brown skin, a cropped ochre flight jacket, blue trousers and fingerless canvas gloves.
cast.voice: Ren speaks briskly, checks knots while talking, and admits uncertainty without losing momentum.
cast.stance: A practical rigging partner who will not pressure the apprentice to disclose private things.

cast.name: Siv
cast.appearance: A small older white woman with fair weathered skin, thick silver hair tied in a bun, green eyes, a sturdy build, a sea-blue coat and a red scarf held by a brass compass pin.
cast.voice: Siv gives precise bearings, challenges confident claims gently, and allows silence while someone checks a measurement.
cast.stance: An island route keeper who wants her community represented accurately.

cast.name: Pavo
cast.appearance: A round-bodied Black adult with deep-brown skin, tightly curled auburn hair, dark eyes, copper freckles, a cream shirt, a teal waistcoat and a canvas delivery satchel.
cast.voice: Pavo speaks in warm, quick phrases and catches himself when a convenient account is not fully true.
cast.stance: A fellow courier hoping for a faster route, able to accept a fair delay.

lift_understood.description: the apprentice knows a non-private truth can provide lift.

margin_owned.description: map limits or errors are acknowledged on the page.

decision_stated.description: the next honest plan is chosen.

beats.title: Canvas Waiting for Breath
beats.sceneBrief: At a sea-cliff dock, Ren helps unpack the apprentice's inheritance: a half-map and an ochre-and-cream balloon with three teal repair panels. The envelope is slack though the rig is sound. A modest truth believed by its speaker tightens it: the observable wind direction or an honest admission that Ren's help is needed both work. Do not demand an emotional secret or speak either statement for the player. Ren can demonstrate with a truthful remark of their own. Establish the nearest safe moorings and the waiting delivery, then offer the first route decision.

choices.label: State the direction you can observe
Admit that you need Ren's help with the rig

beats.hint: The envelope responds to an ordinary observation, not a grand confession.

beats.title: Two Openings in the Cloud
beats.sceneBrief: The map stops short of a cloud bank. One route follows a quicker reef updraft with exposed bearings and fewer places to rest; the other visits a sheltered mail landing where local couriers know the gaps. Ren explains the weather and a practical delivery deadline without turning it into lethal urgency. The chosen approach changes the next location. Both are feasible for an apprentice with help; ordinary truthful observations can maintain lift, and uncertainty is acceptable. The missing map section is a human omission, not evidence that its inhabitants do not exist.

choices.label: Choose the mail landing and local advice

beats.hint: Ren points out the time saved on one route and the resting dock on the other.

beats.title: A Fixed Point in Moving Air
beats.sceneBrief: Ren and the apprentice follow the sea-cliff thermal. Moving clouds make the inherited line look convincing until a fixed dock marker shows its error. Taking bearings together or marking a secure mooring provides direct coastal evidence, both including enough measurements to continue safely to Siv. Keep the balloon's limits consistent: an uncertain statement can be honestly qualified, and any slackening means a controlled landing at the established nearby mooring. This route supplies observations rather than mail records; do not claim the unvisited route also happened.

choices.label: Chart the safe mooring before continuing

beats.hint: A dock marker provides a fixed point against moving cloud.

beats.title: Addresses Beyond the Margin
beats.sceneBrief: Pavo meets Ren and the apprentice at a small post island. His delivery records show regular homes and gardens beyond the inherited chart's blank edge. Comparing the routes or asking who lives there establishes the same useful fact: the map omitted a living community after its mentor's bad old bearing. Pavo initially calls his own route direct, then admits where he has relied on advice rather than measurements. This is an honest correction, not a villain reveal. Local advice provides a safe approach to Siv's shared mooring.

choices.label: Compare Pavo's deliveries with the old chart
Ask who lives beyond the blank section

beats.hint: Pavo's ordinary delivery stamps cover places the inherited map omits.

beats.title: The Line and the Guess
beats.sceneBrief: Safely moored with Siv, the apprentice can compare whichever evidence they actually collected with the mentor's unsupported bearing. The mentor once missed a crossing and left the margin blank rather than record the uncertainty; there is no missing magical key. Siv wants accurate representation, not humiliation. Correcting the demonstrated error or clearly marking what remains unknown both acknowledge the chart's limits. Provide enough local measurement with Siv for a bounded corrected route if the player later chooses publication. An incomplete draft can still be shared honestly, but never presented as fully surveyed.

choices.label: Record the old bearing's error with Siv
Clearly mark what still needs measurement

beats.hint: Siv asks which line was measured and which line was assumed.

beats.title: What the Next Edition Owes
beats.sceneBrief: With the balloon securely moored, Siv, Ren and Pavo lay the chart on a table. The immediate delivery can use Siv's verified approach, a slower known route home, or Pavo's regular service while the apprentice stays to survey. Explain those practical consequences before offering publication, return or collaborative survey. A shared chart must preserve remaining uncertainty even if the earlier choice marked it unknown; no ending requires a false claim of completeness. The balloon responds to an honest plan rather than bravery. Let the player state or choose the intention; never supply a personal confession.

choices.label: Publish a corrected chart with its remaining limits
Admit the route is not ready and return by known moorings
Arrange delivery and stay to survey with the islanders

beats.hint: The balloon lifts for a modest truthful plan as readily as a brave one.

beats.title: A Map with Room for Others
beats.sceneBrief: The apprentice has chosen to publish the corrected chart with its remaining limits marked. Siv's verified approach allows the waiting delivery to arrive, and islanders contribute their own local notes. Blank spaces now mean explicitly unmeasured stretches rather than erased homes. Ren checks the final mooring while Pavo compares the practical route. Close on a chart becoming useful through shared correction. Do not imply a complete survey occurred on either branch or assign the player a triumph speech.
beats.endingTitle: A Map with Room for Others

beats.title: The Honest Way Home
beats.sceneBrief: The apprentice has chosen to return by known moorings with a clearly incomplete chart. Pavo arranges a slower safe delivery through the established service; nobody loses essential supplies for this caution. Ren treats an admitted limit as good navigation. The balloon carries a modest truthful intention toward the familiar sea-cliff dock. End with useful measurements and questions retained for another day, not a failure to be bold or a forced promise to resume.

beats.title: The People Who Know the Wind
beats.sceneBrief: The apprentice has chosen to stay and survey with the islanders while Pavo completes the delivery through his regular service. Siv brings local landmarks, Ren checks the shared gear and Pavo agrees where to bring the next packet. The current story ends with a practical arrangement rather than simulating the entire survey. Future map lines will name what was measured and leave honest room around what was not. The balloon rests securely, its three teal patches visible in afternoon light. Do not decide the player's private feelings about the inheritance.
beats.endingTitle: The People Who Know the Wind
